title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a summarising 'Proposition' for the computations on the surrounding pages (pp. 711–713 of the Longue Marche sequel).

Setting:
- X is a connected, locally connected topos with a geometric point x0.
- Two contexts are allowed. In the discrete one, X is locally simply connected and all coverings are allowed. In the profinite one, 'covering' means profinite covering.
- Γ is a group acting on X by automorphisms. In the profinite case Γ is profinite; Grothendieck notes the continuity hypotheses still need to be made explicit.

Groups and extensions:
- π = π1(X, x0).
- 𝓜 = π1(X, Γ; x0) is the equivariant fundamental group, i.e. π1 of the quotient topos/stack X//Γ. It fits into the extension (*) 1 → π → 𝓜 → Γ → 1.
- One fixes a quotient M of π given by a subgroup of π that is normal in 𝓜. When M is commutative this is the same as a Γ-stable quotient of π_ab = π/[π,π]. Here Γ = 𝓜/π acts on π_ab through the outer action.
- Pushing (*) out gives the quotient extension (**) 1 → M → M̃ → Γ → 1, with M̃ = 𝓜/K. Since M is abelian, Γ acts on M.

Object of study: the category of Γ-equivariant coverings X' of (X, Γ) which, once the Γ-action is forgotten, are connected Galois coverings of X with group M. Such an X' is then an M_X-torsor.

Next page (the answer): the fibre functor X' ↦ E = X'(x0) gives an equivalence with pairs (E, θ). Here E is an M-torsor and θ: M̃ → Aff_Γ(E) is a homomorphism of extensions over Γ → Γ̃ = Im(Γ → Aut M).

Previous page (the point of this): when M^Γ = 0, the data reduce to an M-conjugacy class of splittings of the pulled-back extension. These are Hochschild–Serre type statements on lifting a group action to an abelian Galois covering.

In modern terms this is the standard dictionary: equivariant abelian covers of X correspond to quotients of the orbifold fundamental group of X//Γ. The likely intended use in this manuscript is to construct coverings of moduli stacks of curves equivariantly for a finite symmetry group, or under a Galois action.
errors: Notation clash: the image distinguishes a script 𝓜 = π1(X,Γ;x0) from the roman quotient M of π; the transcription conflates them, and (**) only makes sense with M̃ = 𝓜/K.

The equivalence 'subgroup of π normal in 𝓜 ⇔ Γ-stable quotient of π_ab' holds only once M is required to be abelian. The page assumes this implicitly ('M commutatif') but states it after the equivalence.
Grothendieck himself flags that the continuity hypotheses for profinite Γ are left unstated; no real mathematical error otherwise.

ideas.what: Equivariant fundamental group π1(X,Γ;x0) of a topos with group action, with extension 1→π1(X)→π1(X,Γ)→Γ→1
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the quotient stack/topos X//Γ (orbifold fundamental group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 framework); later Noohi, Zoonekynd for stacks
ideas.where_published: Fundamental group of topoi: SGA1/SGA4; the equivariant version is implicit in SGA1 Exp. V/IX-type arguments

ideas.what: Γ-equivariant abelian Galois coverings classified by fibre M-torsor E plus an extension homomorphism M̃ → Aff_Γ(E)
ideas.modern_name: lifting group actions to abelian covers; equivariant torsors versus splittings of group extensions

deep.surprise_reason: A careful restatement of standard equivariant covering theory, set up in topos language as preparation for the main construction; nothing beyond folklore.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Résumons ces considérations dans une' (likely) rather than '[?] dans un [?]'.
'M = π1(X, Γ; x0)' should be a script 𝓜, distinct from the roman M introduced later.
'Soit [?] M^1 de π, on se donne un quotient by [?] un sous-groupe distingué dans M' should read roughly 'on se donne un quotient M de π, défini par un sous-groupe distingué dans 𝓜'.
The crossed-out line is roughly 'd'où par M̃ = 𝓜/…'; the clean text is 'extension quotient de (*)'.
'à M ab commutatif [?] dans Γ opère sur M' should read roughly 'où M est commutatif, donc Γ opère sur M'.
Final line: 'revêtements 𝔛' de (𝔛, Γ), satisfaisant les conditions' (crossed-out 'torseurs' phrase).
